the performance of the FSO system is affected by the number of hops, turbulence, and geometric loss.
The performance of the multistage FSO communication system is degraded by the turbulence, path loss and pointing errors.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new statistical model and performance analysis of multihop FSo links with pointing errors.
the development of a statistical channel model for the multihop turbulence induced fading FSO channels.
the performance analysis of the multihopt FSO links using a hetero-dyne DPSK scheme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the performance of multihop F SO links with turbulence, pointing errors and path loss can be improved by widening the beam and increasing the relay gain.
the performance of the system is degraded by the increase in the number of hops, turbulence strength, and pointing errors.
the performance of the proposed system can be improved by increasing the number of hops, increasing the aperture diameter, and reducing the pointing errors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multihop system with a fixed relay gain outperforms the multihop channel assisted with channel state information.
the performance of multihop FSo communication systems operating over turbulence channels with pointing errors can be improved by increasing the number of hops while keeping the total length constant.
the proposed multihop FSo system is a viable solution for long distance optical wireless communication systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multihop system with fixed gain relays can be used as an alternative solution for long distance FSO communications.

, for a given number of hops and a given turbulence strength, the outage probability can be reduced by narrowing the beam at the cost of the increased misalignment effects and by increasing the number of hops at the cost of reduced received signal power.
